snippet.title: THE NIGHT MICHAEL JACKSON SHOWED A PRINCE WHY HE IS A KING 🤴 #michaeljackson#prince#jamesbrown#mj
snippet.description:
Here is the breakdown of one of the most legendary—and awkward—moments in pop music history, where the Godfather of Soul inadvertently hosted a live showdown between the King of Pop and the Purple One.

The Date and Setting
 
Date: August 20, 1983
 Location: The Beverly Theater in Los Angeles, California
The Event: A James Brown concert (B.B. King was also there).

How It Went Down
James Brown was in the middle of his set when he noticed Michael Jackson in the VIP section. At the time, MJ was riding the astronomical high of the Thriller album. Brown called Michael up to the stage.

Michael smoothly took the stage, grabbed the mic, sang a few flawless, spontaneous lines of "I Love You, Right On," and then launched into a dazzling, rapid-fire dance routine featuring his signature spins and a razor-sharp moonwalk. The crowd went absolutely wild. Before stepping back into the audience, Michael leaned in and whispered something into James Brown's ear.
Brown then took to the mic and announced, "Michael just told me Prince is in the house!"

How Prince Embarrassed Himself

Prince, whose album *1999* had recently catapulted him to superstardom, had a much rougher time. Following Michael Jackson at his peak is a nearly impossible task, but Prince’s attempt went off the rails almost immediately:

The Entrance:
Prince didn't just walk to the stage; he was awkwardly carried down the aisle piggyback-style by his massive bodyguard, "Big Chick" Huntsberry.

The Guitar Fumble: 
Once on stage, Prince grabbed a guitar, but he struggled to play it. It was out of tune or improperly plugged in, leading to some frantic, disjointed strumming.

The Mic Stand Routine: Prince took his shirt off and attempted some suggestive dance moves with the microphone stand, which failed to land with the same electrifying impact as Michael's crisp routine.
 
The Lamppost Disaster: In a desperate attempt to save the performance and leave an impression, Prince grabbed onto a prop brick-and-mortar lamppost that was part of the stage design. He intended to swing from it dramatically. However, the prop was fake and unanchored. As soon as Prince put his weight on it, the entire lamppost collapsed, sending Prince plummeting into the front rows of the audience.
Humiliated, Prince quickly recovered, abandoned the stage, and practically fled the venue.

Lesser-Known and "Unknown" Facts About the Night
 
It Was Michael's Trap: The showdown wasn't an accident. Michael Jackson essentially set Prince up. Knowing he had just delivered a show-stopping, spontaneous performance, MJ intentionally whispered to James Brown to call Prince up, knowing full well Prince would struggle to follow his act. It was a calculated move in their fierce, unspoken rivalry.
 
The Limo Ambush Rumor: According to legendary producer Quincy Jones (and later corroborated by Michael Jackson in private recordings), Prince was so furious and mortified by the incident that he waited outside the theater in his limousine. Jones claimed Prince's intent was to run Michael over, or at least intimidate him, when MJ exited the building.
 
Michael's Secret Delight: Years later, in a recorded conversation, Michael Jackson reminisced about the event with palpable amusement. He told the interviewer, "He made a fool of himself. He was a joke... People were running and screaming. I was so embarrassed. It was all on video."
 
James Brown's Confusion: If you watch the footage carefully, James Brown looks visibly confused and slightly concerned during Prince's chaotic set, especially when Prince starts removing his clothes and ultimately pulls the set piece down into the crowd.
 
The Missing Glove: Before the lamppost collapse, Prince tossed a prop (often cited as a white glove or a piece of his outfit) into the crowd, seemingly expecting a fan frenzy. According to people in attendance, the crowd mostly just stared at it, compounding the awkwardness of the routine.
